raw_response:
I am not going to spread myself too thin this year. We have 90 mu, but not all five people can stay on the farm because some go out for work, so I need a way that the family can still handle. Wheat and maize are still my main stay because I know that system well, and if one season is a bit weak, the other can make up some. Stevia brings cash if the price is decent, but it needs more hand work, so I will not plant too much of it. I will put 70 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and keep 20 mu in stevia. That feels steady for my family.

For wheat, I will do it much like the better farmers nearby do, not too little fertilizer because I am afraid of losing yield, but not blindly throwing money either. I will sow in early October, use an improved common wheat seed from the local dealer, put most fertilizer at sowing, then topdress once when the crop starts to stand up strong in spring. Since we have well water, I will irrigate when wheat really needs it, but I will watch pumping cost, so probably three times, not more unless spring turns very dry. After wheat harvest in June, I will rush to put summer maize on that same 70 mu right away, because that window is always tight here. For maize I will use hybrid seed, do simple tillage or rotary work after wheat, and give two fertilizer applications. Stevia I will keep on 20 mu only, because it needs more care and more hands. I will use decent seedlings, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate when it looks dry, and plan for more hand labor there than wheat or maize.
